newsitem.title: USA: Genetics stock jumps after American Home deal.
newsitem.headline: Genetics stock jumps after American Home deal.

text.p: The stock of Genetics Institute Inc. soared Wednesday after American Home Products Corp. said it would buy the rest of Genetics Institute Inc. for about $1 billion, or $85 a share.
Shares of Genetics Institute, a Cambridge, Mass.-based biotechnology company, jumped $22.75 to $84.50 on Nasdaq, where the gain of nearly 37 percent was one of the biggest of the session.

American Home, the maker of Advil and Anacin, Robitussin and a host of prescription drugs, said late Tuesday it would buy the 40 percent of Genetics Institute it does not already own at the current exercise price of $85 a share.
Madison, N.J.-based American Home bought 60 percent of Genetics Institute in 1992 for $666 million and received an option to acquire the rest.

The move by American Home came less than a week after a Food and Drug Administration advisory panel voted to recommend approval of Genetics Institute's blood clotting therapy, known as BeneFix, for haemophilia B.
American Home Products stock added $1.125 to $60.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.

American Home also said it would take a $700 million charge this year to write off research and development expenses and a $300 million charge for goodwill. The announcement on Tuesday came after the close of regular trading.
